commitResults.messageTitle: Limit email and tag length and the number of tags
commitResults.messageBody:
A very long email or hyphenated tag overflowed the stack inside the
validation regex. The error was not caught, so the command failed with
no message and the previous result stayed on screen. There was also no
limit on email length or on how many tags a student could have.

Let's check the length before the regex runs, capping emails at 254
characters (the RFC 5321 limit) and tags at 30, and allow at most 10
tags per student. Over-long input now gets the normal error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UML diagrams for delete all and editsession
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG explains delete all and editsession in text only. Readers cannot
see that delete all keeps groups and sessions, or that editsession
rebuilds every student's attendance for the edited session.

Let's add an activity diagram for delete all and a sequence diagram for
editsession, and show them in their DG sections.

This PR is meant to cover delete all only.

Let's remove the editsession diagram and its DG reference, keeping the
delete all activity diagram.
Add an activity diagram for delete all

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep loading saved data that exceeds new limits
commitResults.messageBody:
The email and tag length limits were checked in Email and Tag, which
the JSON loader also uses. A roster saved by v1.5 with a 31-character
tag or a 255-character email therefore failed to load, and Roster
started with an empty roster that a later save could write over.

Let's check the limits in ParserUtil instead, so they apply only to
new command input, and keep the model validators as lenient as before.

The length check had also stopped the validation regexes overflowing
the stack on very long input. Let's rewrite both regexes without a
repeated group, which is what caused the overflow. The new patterns
accept exactly the same strings as the old ones.

commitResults.messageTitle: Start Roster even with invalid window preferences
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited preferences.json could stop Roster from starting, and
because the file is saved back unchanged, it failed on every later
launch too:

* A negative window width or height made JavaFX throw while the main
  window was being sized, so Roster showed a fatal error and quit.
* "guiSettings": null was written straight into the field, skipping
  the setter's null check, so copying the preferences threw a
  NullPointerException during start-up.

Other invalid preferences already fall back to the defaults. Let's do
the same for these two cases: use the default window size when the
saved one is negative or infinite, and restore the default settings
when the file holds null.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test each invalid window size dimension separately
commitResults.messageBody:
The size check combines four conditions, but the tests only made the
width invalid, so the height conditions were never false on their own
and Codecov reported them as partly covered.

Let's test a negative and an infinite value for each dimension.
Start Roster even with invalid window preferences

commitResults.messageTitle: Document name suggestions in both guides
commitResults.messageBody:
Neither guide explains how a failed search
picks the names it offers. The developer guide
never names NameSimilarityScorer or
TopSimilarStudents, and the user guide buries
the behaviour in a bullet about successful
searches, quoting none of the feedback.

A reader cannot tell why Jaro-Winkler was
chosen over an edit distance, where the 0.85
threshold came from, or what counts as a close
name. The find use case stops at 'no students
were found'.

Describe the feature in both guides, add a
sequence diagram, and extend the use case.

The threshold is recorded with the scores it
was set from, measured rather than recalled,
including the pair it separates and a name it
wrongly admits. A limit documented with its
cost can be retuned later; a bare number
cannot.

Also correct TopSimilarStudents, which still
claimed near misses cost no extra pass. That
stopped being true when scoring moved to after
the search.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UML diagrams and doc for UI navigation and student detail panel

commitResults.messageBody:
Five members in the main source set have no
caller, and two commented-out TODO tests have
never run.

Unreachable code still has to be read and kept
correct. A reader cannot tell at a glance that
it is unused, so it costs attention on every
pass without doing anything in return.

Delete FileUtil.createIfMissing with the private
helper only it called, MainWindow's
getPersonListPanel accessor, ResultDisplay's
setFeedbackToUser alias, the unread copyButton
and detailPane fields, and the two TODO tests
in JsonUtilTest.

Delete rather than suppress, because nothing
here is a seam kept for a planned use. Where a
field was the last user of an import, the
import goes too, which checkstyle would
otherwise reject.

The fx:id attributes stay in the FXML. The CSS
rules and the lookup in StudentDetailUiTest
address those nodes by id, and FXMLLoader sets
a node's id from its fx:id, so only the Java
field was unused.

Helpers reached solely by tests are left alone.
NameSimilarityScorer.isSimilar and
Suggestion.apply each name an idea their tests
would otherwise spell out by hand, so removing
them would cost more than it saves.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the detail panel's scroll position
commitResults.messageBody:
Opening a student scrolls the panel to the top,
and so does every later command on that student,
because show() resets the scroll whenever it
rebuilds the panel's contents.

On a laptop screen the panel overflows, so a
tutor reading attendance near the bottom is sent
back to the top by their own comment or mark.
The student they are reading has not changed,
only one part of what is shown.

Reset the scroll only when a different student
is opened, and otherwise put the panel back
where the reader left it.

Keep the position in pixels rather than as the
proportion vvalue holds. A new note or a newly
marked session makes the contents taller, and
the same proportion of a taller panel is a
different place, so a proportion would drift.

Apply it twice: once from the heights the last
layout measured, and again on the next
post-layout pulse, since the rebuilt height is
not known before then. The pulse listener is
cancelled on hide and before each rebuild.

The app still reports V1.5, ten diagrams have
changed since v1.5 without a cache-buster on
their reference, the screenshot has one that was
never bumped, and docs/team holds the sample
member page the template shipped with.

A reference whose URL has not changed is served
from the cache, so a reader who saw the site
during v1.5 keeps seeing the old picture however
many times the file behind it is replaced. The
screenshot is the visible case today.

Report V1.6, mark the changed diagrams and the
screenshot with the new version, and drop the
sample member page.

Leave the seven references that already carry
v1.5 alone. Those images have not changed since
the tag, so bumping them would discard a cached
copy that is still correct, and would suggest
they were part of this release.

The sample page is the last file under
docs/team, nothing links to it, and AboutUs
names no portfolio pages, so removing it leaves
no gap behind.
Prepare the v1.6 release
